messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT INC-7891 created — high error-rate on economy tier in eu-west. Paging oncall @eric_oncall :rotating_light:
ops-bot: brief: 45% increase in 5xxs, request latency 2.3x baseline for short chats. Affected routes: /v1/generate (economy), /v1/embeddings (economy).

amanda_infra: seeing request queueing on GPU pools for economy lane in eu-west-1. KV-cache hit rate normal. Batches bigger than usual.

eric_oncall: on it — joining call now. Can someone pull the routing policy counters?

sre_sarah: grabbed live metrics: latency spike aligns with sudden surge from a single customer CID 0x4f3e. Smart-routing shows 60% of their traffic pinned to economy lane due to cost preference.

lisa_product: customer 0x4f3e is a heavy embedder, likely low-prioritization preference. They're on a monthly plan. They started a job ~15m ago, steady high qps.

eric_oncall: ok, two immediate mitigations on my list: (1) apply short-term rate limit per-customer for economy tier, (2) steer a portion of economy requests to standard tier for eu-west only as a graceful degradation. Thoughts?

amanda_infra: agree. Quick knobs: we can lower economy lane per-cust burst from 200 -> 50 and set per-cust qps soft cap 20 for 10m. Then add a steer policy: if economy queue_latency > 200ms then route 30% to standard (same region).

sre_sarah: note: steering to standard will increase cost. We need to evaluate customer SLA exposure. If we rate-limit, they'll see 429s for a bit.

lisa_product: prefer steer over hard 429s for user-facing product. But need to notify downstream billing/CS.

devex_jay: putting a quick snippet for the steer rule to apply in the console (use canary label so we can revert):

```
policy: {
  id: "temp-eu-economy-steer-2319876543",
  trigger: { queue_latency_ms: ">200" },
  action: {
    steer_percentage: 30,
    target_tier: "standard",
    canary: true,
    duration: "15m"
  }
}
```

eric_oncall: applying rate-limit first. Running:

```
curl -X POST https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/policies/rate_limit \
  -d '{"scope":"customer:0x4f3e","tier":"economy","burst":50,"qps":20,"ttl":"10m"}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```

ops-bot: policy rate_limit applied (id rl-2319876550) by eric_oncall.

amanda_infra: confirmed new token bucket in place. Token refill steady. Economy request 5xxs dropping from 45% -> 18% after rate-limit — good sign.

eric_oncall: now applying steer canary to 30% in eu-west.

ops-bot: policy temp-eu-economy-steer-2319876543 deployed in canary mode to eu-west (30% steer to standard).

sre_sarah: watching metrics — standard tier CPU/GPU load rising but still within buffer. Latency on economy is improving, 5xxs now 10%.

lisa_product: tagging @cs-team and billing: heads-up that we may route to standard which will incur higher cost for that customer for the next 15m. Please prepare a message if this becomes a billing-affecting incident.

amanda_infra: small note — KV cache misses increased slightly on standard because model sharding differs; should be transient.

eric_oncall: good. Let's keep the steer on for 15m, monitor closely. If standard spikes, we fallback to tightening the steer (reduce to 10%) or enable temporary model-variant with higher quantization (lower perf but lower cost).

devex_jay: reminder: we have a prebuilt rollback: `policy disable temp-eu-economy-steer-2319876543`

ops-bot: alert threshold crossed: standard tier GPU utilization > 70% in eu-west. current: 74%. Approaching autoscale threshold.

sre_sarah: autoscale headroom should cover short spike but set an econ fallback plan now: if standard GPU util > 78% for 3m, then reduce steer to 10% and enable per-cust elevated qps only for trusted customers.

eric_oncall: agreed. I'm enabling the dynamic fallback rule.

```
policy update temp-eu-economy-steer-2319876543 {
  fallback_trigger: { gpu_util_pct: ">78", duration: "3m" },
  fallback_action: { steer_percentage: 10 }
}
```

ops-bot: policy updated with fallback.

amanda_infra: after fallback rule, standard GPU util plateaued and started easing. economy 5xxs back to baseline ~2%.

lisa_product: CS confirmed they'll reach out to 0x4f3e if billing delta > $X threshold. No urgent customer complaint right now.

eric_oncall: plan for handoff in 30m: continue monitoring, leave steer policy active for full 15m window, leave rate-limit active for 10m. I'll synthesize a short handoff note for next oncall. Any final checks?

sre_sarah: add to incident timeline: root cause is high-volume embed job pinned to economy by cost preference + lack of per-cust burst protection for economy. Recommend: (a) permanent per-cust burst caps on economy, (b) automatic cross-tier steering for prolonged queueing, (c) telemetry flag for oversized embed jobs.

amanda_infra: creating a follow-up ticket for config defaults and infra autoscale rule tuning.

ops-bot: INC-7891 status: mitigation in place (rate-limit + canary steer). Next update in 15m or on significant change.

eric_oncall: HANDOFF summary for next oncall (@sre_sarah will triage if escalated):
- What happened: economy lane in eu-west experienced surge from single customer causing latency and 5xxs.
- What we did: applied per-customer rate-limit (burst 50, qps 20, ttl 10m) and deployed a canary steer (30% to standard) with dynamic fallback to 10%.
- Current state: economy 5xxs down to ~2%, standard util stabilized <75%, no customer-facing escalations yet.
- Follow-ups: ticket INF-3425 for policy defaults; product to consider soft-limits and customer warnings; CS to monitor billing impact.

sre_sarah: ACK. I'll take point if it resurfaces.

eric_oncall: leaving a final note before stepping off: set `ops:incident:INC-7891` channel retention to 72h and attach dashboards. stepping off in 25m.

ops-bot: eric_oncall has acknowledged and set incident state to MONITORING.

lisa_product: thanks all. Good policies here — we should bake the steering fallback into runbooks.

devex_jay: +1. I'll draft a runbook snippet and circulate.

ops-bot: INCIDENT INC-7891 last update at 2319877210.
